title: Tour: the water treatment plant, from the river to the demineralised water tank

p: Follow the water from the river through the intake, the clarifiers and filters, reverse osmosis, the degasser and the mixed beds to the demineralised water the HRSG is fed with.

text: The bar screen (
) keeps logs and rubbish out of the intake channel; the travelling band screens behind it (
) catch what is larger than 9.5 mm.
Three vertical raw water pumps (
) stand over the wet well, two running. They send the river water through the buried raw water main (
) to the treatment plant.
The rapid mixer (
) mixes the coagulant into the water in seconds: the fine clay particles start to gather into flocs.
The clarifiers (
) let the flocs settle; the clear water spills over the weirs into the launder round the wall. Its bridge, up the stair, carries the rake's drive.
The gravity filters (
): six cells of sand and anthracite, their valves in the gallery under the deck, seen from its ends. A filter whose head loss grows is backwashed with air and water.
The filtered water tank (
) feeds the cooling tower makeup pumps (
) and the service water pumps, which also feed the RO.
Cartridge filters (
) of 5 µm protect the membranes; sodium bisulphite has taken the chlorine out before them.
The high-pressure pump (
) raises the feed to about 12 bar; the RO train (
) passes three quarters of it through the membranes as permeate.
The degasser (
) blows the carbon dioxide out of the permeate before the mixed beds.
The mixed beds (
) polish the water to under 0.1 µS/cm.
The demineralised water tanks (
) store about four days of the plant's needs; the transfer pumps (
) send it to the train.
The plant's demineralised water tank (
) beside the auxiliary boiler: the makeup of the water-steam cycle comes from here.
